For carbon and alloy steel bolts, the fi: For carbon and alloy steel bolts, the first number multiplied by 100 gives nominal tensile strength in MPa. The second number divided by 10 gives the nominal yield-to-tensile ratio. Class 8.8 therefore represents 800 MPa nominal tensile strength and a nominal ratio of 0.8.
These numbers explain the designation; t: These numbers explain the designation; they are not a complete acceptance specification. Required minimum properties and test methods depend on the applicable standard, diameter and product geometry.
Use this table to understand markings, n: Use this table to understand markings, not to calculate a safe working load or an installation torque. MPa is equivalent to N/mm².
A higher class is not automatically a be: A higher class is not automatically a better replacement. Check the specified preload, mating nut, washer, thread engagement, coating and service environment together. Changing the lubricant or finish can change the torque needed to achieve the intended clamp force.
Low and countersunk heads may have reduc: Low and countersunk heads may have reduced loadability. For a countersunk socket screw, check its product standard as well as its property class before applying data from a conventional hex bolt.
What to include in your RFQ: What to include in your RFQ
State the product standard, thread diame: State the product standard, thread diameter and pitch, length, property class, finish and quantity. Include the drawing revision and required inspection documents. If replacing an existing fastener, provide its markings and assembly requirements rather than relying on a photograph alone.
A purchasing guide to the M39–M64 scope,: A purchasing guide to the M39–M64 scope, assembly requirements and documentation for GB/T 32076.7.
GB/T 32076.7-2015 covers M39–M64 large-w: GB/T 32076.7-2015 covers M39–M64 large-width-across-flats hexagon bolt and nut assemblies for preloaded structural connections. It is not a general specification for every high strength bolt or every metric diameter.
The official Chinese standard record lis: The official Chinese standard record lists publication on 9 October 2015 and implementation on 1 June 2016. Identify the required edition in the purchase specification and check the project documents before ordering.
Describe the bolt and nut combination, a: Describe the bolt and nut combination, and identify any washers required by the project. State the diameter, pitch, length, property class, finish and required quantities for each component. A bolt that looks similar is not evidence that the complete assembly meets the same requirements.
Keep delivery identification and inspect: Keep delivery identification and inspection records with the supplied lots. When reviewing alternatives, compare dimensional and assembly requirements before agreeing to substitute another standard.
A strength class alone does not establis: A strength class alone does not establish an installation torque. Ask the project engineer to identify the required preload, tightening method and acceptance checks. Confirm that any supplied lubrication and coating match the agreed installation procedure.
Do not assume that a torque value used o: Do not assume that a torque value used on a smaller bolt, another coating or a different assembly can be scaled directly to an M39–M64 connection.
Attach the approved drawing and standard: Attach the approved drawing and standard edition. Ask the supplier to confirm dimensional compliance, assembly identification, required mechanical tests, coating details and traceability documents. Record any proposed deviation explicitly so that the project team can review it before manufacture.
Compare coating processes, thread fit an: Compare coating processes, thread fit and hydrogen-embrittlement considerations before requesting a fastener quotation.
ISO 4042 addresses electroplated coating: ISO 4042 addresses electroplated coating systems for fasteners, including zinc and zinc alloys. A finish specification should identify the coating system, any conversion layer, sealer and lubricant, rather than only a colour.
The standard includes requirements and r: The standard includes requirements and recommendations to reduce hydrogen-embrittlement risk. For high strength fasteners, agree the process controls and applicable verification with the supplier before choosing an electroplated finish.
ISO 10684 covers spun hot-dip galvanized: ISO 10684 covers spun hot-dip galvanized coatings on coarse-threaded steel fasteners from M8 to M64, up to class 10.9 for bolts, screws and studs and class 12 for nuts. Its scope should not be extended automatically to class 12.9 bolts.
Specify the mating thread arrangement an: Specify the mating thread arrangement and check fit after coating. The coating and nut thread allowances belong in the assembly specification, not just in a note describing the desired appearance.
ISO 10683 covers non-electrolytically ap: ISO 10683 covers non-electrolytically applied zinc flake systems. These systems are used on high strength fasteners to address internal hydrogen-embrittlement concerns associated with coating processes. Preparation and application still need controlled procedures.
Confirm the complete coating system, inc: Confirm the complete coating system, including topcoat and lubricant. A trade name alone does not define corrosion performance, friction behaviour or suitability for the intended joint.
Compare quotations on the same basis: Compare quotations on the same basis
Give each supplier the same service envi: Give each supplier the same service environment, corrosion test and acceptance criteria, thread-fit requirements, friction requirements and quantity. Ask for the process specification and relevant test results. Compare the quoted coating system and inspection scope, not colour or price alone.
Specify the material standard, heat-trea: Specify the material standard, heat-treatment condition and finished-fastener requirements when sourcing chromium-molybdenum steel fasteners.
Start with the exact material designatio: Start with the exact material designation
Write the material grade together with i: Write the material grade together with its governing standard and delivery condition. Avoid specifying only “alloy steel” when the drawing requires a particular chemistry or mechanical performance.
42CrMo, 42CrMo4 and SAE 4140 are related: 42CrMo, 42CrMo4 and SAE 4140 are related designations, but they should not be accepted as automatic substitutes. Compare the governing specifications, chemical limits, product form and required tests before approving a substitution. Ovako lists 4140 among similar designations for 42CrMo4 and identifies specific variants separately.

Ovako describes 42CrMo4 as a quenching a: Ovako describes 42CrMo4 as a quenching and tempering steel and reports mechanical properties by delivery condition and bar diameter. This illustrates why a grade name alone does not determine the properties of every finished part.

Galling can occur when mating threads ad: Galling can occur when mating threads adhere under friction. Stainless steel corrosion resistance does not prevent this assembly problem. A seized thread may damage both components; increasing force is not a reliable remedy.

Discuss compatible lubrication or surfac: Discuss compatible lubrication or surface treatments for the application. Record the agreed condition in the purchasing specification. Validate the tightening procedure with that condition; a lubricant change should not inherit an unreviewed torque setting.

Hydrogen embrittlement can cause delayed: Hydrogen embrittlement can cause delayed failure after assembly. Acid cleaning and electroplating can introduce hydrogen into susceptible fasteners. A clean appearance or completed assembly does not establish that this risk has been controlled.
Provide the fastener material and proper: Provide the fastener material and property requirements alongside the coating specification. Ask for a process review, applicable standards and documented controls. Treat hydrogen relief as a qualified process requirement, rather than an automatic guarantee against failure.
Agree on process records, required testi: Agree on process records, required testing and sample approval before manufacture. Keep corrosion protection, thread fit and assembly requirements in the same review. Final process selection depends on the product and application; this article supplies an RFQ checklist, not a blanket coating approval.
